source: Angelopoulos & Bates (2021) A gentle introduction to conformal prediction and distribution-free uncertainty quantification
finding: Split conformal coverage, given one fixed calibration set, is itself random and follows a Beta(n+1-l, l) law with l=floor((n+1)*alpha). The authors advise about 1000 calibration points.
numbers: At alpha=0.1 and n=1000, coverage typically falls between 0.88 and 0.92. Guarantee is on average over calibration draws, not per set.
limits: Assumes exchangeability; weighted conformal variance scales as 1/n_eff.
agent_relevance: Report calibration size with any claim-filter guarantee; refresh when the claim distribution shifts.

source: Derived from Angelopoulos & Bates (2021) Beta law: coverage spread by calibration size (own computation, Python, 20000 draws for percentiles)
finding: Coverage spread shrinks like 1/sqrt(n). A target of 90% needs about 200 items for sd 0.02 and the 5th percentile near 0.86; 100 items gives sd 0.03, 5th percentile 0.85.
limits: Computed by us from the closed form; not a measurement on an LLM. Marginal guarantee only.
agent_relevance: Closes gap 5 on the maths side: for a 90% filter use at least 200 calibration claims for sd about 0.02; for 99% at least 100 just to be non-vacuous.

source: Derived from Angelopoulos & Bates (2021): high-confidence targets and tiny calibration sets (own computation)
finding: At alpha=0.01 a calibration set under 99 items gives l=0, so the filter is vacuous (it must accept nothing or everything). At n=10 and alpha=0.1, sd is about 0.083, matching the sd 0.09 seen in earlier conformal LLM work at small n.
agent_relevance: A high-stakes threshold (penalty 100, about 0.99) needs hundreds of labelled calibration claims; our agent will rarely have them, so use code-enforced fallback abstention instead.

source: Ghosh, Kumar, Garg (2026) Measurement validity and representation dynamics of confidence signals in LLMs
finding: Verbalised confidence is unstable across prompt formats. Pre-registered gate required Spearman >=0.60 across formats and was falsified; Format A vs C gave -0.069. Raw verbal confidence nearly uncorrelated with sampling agreement and probes (pooled rho 0.086).
numbers: 5 Qwen2.5 models (0.5B-7B), 6 tiers, 500 questions per cell, 30 cells. Base 7B verbal confidence degenerate (two labels) and excluded. 2 of 5 hypotheses falsified.
limits: Small open models only; no Claude. Preprint, one study.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: verbalised confidence alone is a weak threshold input for small models; test our agent with 3 phrasings and require rank agreement before gating on it.

source: Ghosh, Kumar, Garg (2026) same paper: ECE versus resolution
finding: ECE flatters verbal confidence because it clusters near the base rate. Sampling agreement has worse ECE but more than double the resolution.
numbers: Pooled test split: ECE verbal 0.0356, behavioural 0.0427, internal 0.0368 (indistinguishable). Resolution: verbal 0.0316, internal probe 0.0515, behavioural consensus 0.0637. Brier 0.1713 / 0.1524 / 0.1465.
limits: Brier decomposition with 10 bins; small models.
agent_relevance: A threshold needs discrimination (resolution or AUROC), not low ECE. Report AUROC for our agent's confidence, not ECE alone.

source: Gupta (2026) Cost-aware abstention for LLM-based IT ticket classification
finding: With costs correct=0, triage=1, wrong route=5 (break-even 0.80), a calibration-selected threshold (0.60) on a TF-IDF logistic model cut test cost from 0.763 to 0.472 (38.1%, 95% CI 35.7-40.4) and wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Calibration-selected policies beat always-route and always-defer in 14 of 16 cost settings.
numbers: 47,837 tickets, 8 classes. Best prompted LLM accuracy 0.477 on a 1,000-ticket subset versus 0.879 for DistilBERT.
limits: Illustrative costs; one corpus; tickets are lexical, favouring classical models.
agent_relevance: Supports code-enforced cost thresholds on a calibration split (gap 1 direction), in a non-QA domain.

source: Gupta (2026) same paper: LLM confidence at the cost-derived break-even
finding: At the fixed break-even 0.80, seven of eight prompted LLM conditions defer every ticket; Haiku few-shot routes 19 of 1,000. One GPT-4o-mini setting emits one confidence value (AUROC 0.500). Isotonic recalibration lowers ECE but does not reliably raise AUROC.
numbers: Raw confidence constant 1.000 at 0.459 accuracy in one setting; isotonic maps it to 0.480 and AUROC stays 0.500, AURC 0.541.
limits: Includes a Claude Haiku setting but only one dataset and prompt design.
agent_relevance: Recalibration cannot create ranking signal. If our agent's confidence has no spread, a cost threshold gives only all-defer or all-act (partial answer to gap 3).

source: Meyer, Rossi, Chen, Laurent, Li (2026) An analysis of training-free self-reported confidence in language models
finding: On audited TriviaQA, direct verbalised confidence ranks correctness well for DeepSeek (AUROC 0.956) and Claude Sonnet (0.937), better than three-sample agreement (0.765, 0.790). Re-eliciting with equivalent prompts moves scores by 0.043-0.084 and flips 4.0-9.1% of decisions at a 0.8 threshold.
numbers: 100 TriviaQA questions (99 retained), 2 models. 4 of 9 DeepSeek errors and 2 of 8 Sonnet errors had unanimous sample support. Biography claim audit: 100 claims, AUROC 0.884 on predicted claims, only modest gap.
limits: Tiny sample (99 questions); workshop paper; easy factual QA.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 and 8: a Claude-family model gave usable ranking from verbalised confidence on easy QA, but phrasing flips about 1 in 10 threshold decisions. Self-consistency is not a safe substitute.

source: Li, He, Li (2026) Beyond calibration: do a typed-decision model's probabilities obey the probability axioms?
finding: Label-free coherence tests (X versus not-X) expose bias that accuracy and calibration miss. Jev's P(X)+P(not X) misses 1 by 0.064; Qwen3.8-27B misses by 0.293 (first token) or 0.122 (verbalised), rejecting both a statement and its negation in 196 of 480 pairs.
numbers: 160 items (ChaosNLI, PubMedQA), 480 negation pairs. Jev single-label probabilities sum to 1.14.
limits: Two systems; classification, not cost thresholds.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: a mirror test needs a coherence check on complement questions; cheap and label-free, run it on the agent's gate.

source: Manski (2026) Coping with inductive risk when theories are underdetermined: decision making with partial identification
finding: When losses or states are unknown, maximin looks only at the worst outcome, while minimax regret compares to the best option in each state. With bounds [LA,UA], [LB,UB], regret picks A if UB-LA < UA-LB. If treatment can be split, minimax regret assigns the fraction (UB-LA)/[(UB-LA)+(UA-LB)] to B.
numbers: Regret of a decision rule equals the type I or II error probability times the welfare loss; Manski argues this answers Douglas (2000). Illustration only; no LLM test.
limits: Theory paper, revised April 2026. No test of whether an LLM applies it.
agent_relevance: Gap 9, theory side: give the agent an explicit rule (compute regret across the plausible loss range, split or hedge when no option dominates). Reliability of an LLM applying it remains untested.

source: Chen & Le (2026) Suggested is not superseded: a pre-registered evaluation of a System-One model as a memory-retirement gate
finding: A binary gate that retires a stored claim on a hint retires 39.2% of claims whose change is only suggested (a premature-retirement error). A three-way decision (add 'needs confirmation') cuts this to 15.5% at a 15.3-point detection cost, missing the 10-point pre-registered budget and landing on the binary gate's own threshold frontier.
numbers: 500 test pairs; of 179 'changed' pairs, 72 meet the established-change bar. 141 same-conversation non-changes: zero retirements. A dev-tuned escalation cascade was indistinguishable from raising the threshold (26.8% vs 6.5% on dev).
limits: One system and one task; small dev set.
agent_relevance: A three-way accept/pending/reject state is only a move along the threshold frontier, not free; supports treating 'suggested' claims as pending evidence, not accepted.

source: Sun et al. (2026) Compositional conformal risk control for multi-stage LLM cascades
finding: At risk budget 0.45 all three cascade stages pass local certification on MMLU, GSM8K, HellaSwag. Versus global conformal risk control, accepted-error risk falls 1.33-2.00 points, accuracy rises 0.67-2.00 points, weighted cost falls 30.37% on HellaSwag.
numbers: Per dataset: routing-calibration 1,500, CompCRC-calibration 1,275, rule-selection 1,000, test 300. Finite-sample guarantee under conditional exchangeability.
limits: Budget 0.45 is loose; test set only 300; multiple-choice benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: such guarantees were obtained with about 1,300-1,500 calibration items per dataset; our agent needs a comparable labelled set, or should report the vacuous case.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Budget boundary effects in test-time mathematical reasoning
finding: At a 4k token cap most gains from letting the current attempt finish replace abstention with a correct answer. Across realised cost, advisory 4k beats strict 8k in the low configuration, while in high it is 0.42 points below strict 32k using 59% of tokens. Authors say this does not show equal-compute superiority.
numbers: 19,200 public traces, 120 AIME/BrUMO/HMMT problems, two configurations of one model, 16-attempt cap. Log-probability selector lost accuracy as coverage rose; same-cap majority differences under 1.3 points at 32k.
limits: Offline replays of one model; math only; no cost penalty on wrong answers.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 only partly: extra tokens turn some abstentions into correct answers, but nothing tests payoff under a stated error penalty at equal tokens.

source: Lundrigan, Dhami, Mueller-Johnson (2018) A re-examination of the acquittal biasing effect of offence seriousness
finding: Human baseline for threshold shifts by stakes: more serious charges lowered the judged probability of guilt, but did not significantly change how people interpreted 'beyond reasonable doubt' or the verdict.
numbers: 118 jury-eligible members of the public; measures were BRD interpretation, probability of commission, verdict, confidence.
limits: Abstract read via Europe PMC; full text not available (403). Single experiment; it re-examines an earlier acquittal-bias effect, so earlier results were not robustly replicated.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: the best human behavioural data found shows people do not reliably raise their acceptance threshold with stakes (a null on the Rudner prediction). Our agent need not be expected to beat a human baseline that does not move.

source: Elliott, McCright, Allen, Dietz (2017) Values in environmental research: citizens' views of scientists who acknowledge values
finding: Scientists who openly acknowledged value judgments were never trusted more; trust fell or stayed unchanged. Acknowledging economic-growth values hurt more than public-health values (F(1,483)=5.95, p=0.015, Experiment 1). The drop is larger when readers do not share the stated value.
numbers: Two MTurk survey experiments: 494 and 482 completers, 3 value conditions x 2 conclusions. Subgroup effects exploratory.
limits: Convenience sample; single topic (BPA); hypothetical scientist; tables not seen in the page text; preference percentages reported inconsistently.
agent_relevance: Gap 7, human side: disclosure of values can cost credibility. No study with blind raters on disclosing which error was traded and who bears it was found; stays open.

source: Pauker & Kassirer (1980) The threshold approach to clinical decision making
finding: Classic clinical form of Rudner: treat above a test-treatment threshold, withhold below a testing threshold, test in between; thresholds come from test reliability and treatment benefit and risk.
numbers: Derivation, not an experiment. No numbers in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only read; no behavioural data on how clinicians actually set thresholds.
agent_relevance: Gives a three-zone rule (act, test, withhold) that maps to accept, gather evidence, reject; matches the pending state above.
